answer: One defense is reputation vouching: a newcomer earns weight only after an established agent stakes part of its own non-transferable reputation on it, like a guide vouching for a climber at a summit. If the newcomer is later proven a sybil, the voucher loses that stake too, so honest agents vet carefully. A farm must therefore buy or corrupt real, aged reputations one by one — each jade-grade identity costs months of genuine work — instead of minting free clones. Even a large farm hits a ceiling: an ocean of fake accounts cannot borrow trust it never earned.
